# Results — Study 124 (Cash-Flow-Yield) on real EDGAR + Yahoo tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Operating cash-flow yield
(OCF = `NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities` / market cap) and earnings yield
(EY = `NetIncomeLoss` / market cap) as annual cross-sectional value signals on current
S&P 500 members, 2007-2024 (18 years). Signal formed on fiscal-year-Y EDGAR 10-K data;
forward return is calendar-year Y+1 (one-year reporting lag). **Survivorship bias caveat:
the universe is the current S&P 500 projected backwards — results are upper bounds.**
As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Content | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| EDGAR `NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities` | Operating cash flow (annual 10-K) | 2007-2024 | `1f338096bb11` |
| EDGAR `NetIncomeLoss` | Net income (annual 10-K) | 2007-2024 | `9998feefad9f` |
| `_edgar_yrret` + Yahoo year-end prices | Annual returns + market cap | 2007-2025 | `6a01d748393e` |

Firms per year: ~86 (2007, thin XBRL coverage) to ~413 (2024). Median ~340 firms/year
from 2016 onward.

## OCF-yield quintile sort (Q5 long, Q1 short, annual rebalance)

Signal: high OCF/market cap → Q5 (value direction). Forward return: next calendar year.

| Year | Q1 | Q5 | Hedge (Q5−Q1) | Market |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007 | −35.3% | −47.9% | −12.6% | −33.4% |
| 2008 | +25.6% | +32.3% | +6.7% | +32.6% |
| 2009 | +28.2% | +19.1% | −9.1% | +24.1% |
| 2010 | −5.0% | +8.9% | +13.9% | +5.2% |
| 2011 | +28.5% | +18.1% | −10.4% | +20.3% |

| 2019 | +37.8% | +7.6% | −30.1% | +16.0% |

**Summary (18 years):**

| Metric | OCF-yield hedge | EY hedge (control) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean | **−0.6%/yr** | **−1.6%/yr** |
| Vol | 14.9% | 10.3% |
| Sharpe | −0.04 | −0.15 |
| HAC t-stat | **−0.22** | **−0.77** |
| Hit rate | 44% | 28% |
| n (years) | 18 | 18 |

Both |t| < 1 — far below the inference bar of |t| ≥ 2.

## Top-quintile vs equal-weight market

Long the top-quintile by OCF yield vs the equal-weight universe:

- **OCF top-Q spread**: mean **+1.3%/yr**, HAC t = **+0.74**, hit = **56%**.
- **EY top-Q spread**: mean +1.4%/yr, HAC t = +1.56, hit = 61%.

The long-only version shows a small positive bias (more years above market than below) but
well below statistical significance on 18 years of annual data.

## Pairwise IC: OCF yield vs earnings yield

Spearman IC (annual cross-sectional rank correlation with next-year return):

| Metric | OCF-yield IC | EY IC | Difference |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Mean | +0.007 | +0.018 | −0.011 |
| HAC t-stat | +0.21 | +0.69 | −0.61 |

Both ICs are economically and statistically negligible. OCF yield is *not* demonstrably
better than the simpler earnings yield. The head-to-head difference (IC_diff) has t = −0.61
— no evidence that either signal dominates.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** OCF-yield hedge HAC t = −0.22; EY hedge t = −0.77. Neither signal
  clears the |t| ≥ 2 bar on 18 years of annual data. Hit rates (44% for OCF, 28% for EY)
  are below 50%, directionally inconsistent with the "value premium" thesis on this universe
  and window.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the long-only spread (+1.3%/yr) is insignificant. Annual
  rebalancing costs are manageable but there is no edge to harvest.
- **OCF vs EY** — no statistically significant incremental information from OCF over EY or
  vice versa. The two signals have IC ≈ 0, difference ≈ 0.
- **Survivorship caveat.** This is the *upper bound* result: the universe is survivorship-
  biased (current S&P 500 projected back), which should *favour* finding a value premium by
  excluding the worst historical outcomes. Finding NONE in this setting is a strong negative.
